$comment: Figma layer path (as in spec.json) -> element inside the entry's target (.ds-prompt-library).

Templates.$why: Figma draws the 1 px line between the columns as its own layer; in code it is the list's right border (251 px), so the template column starts at the same place. The list is its own element in code, 4 px under the search like Figma's rows are 4 px apart.

Search.$why: Input's own check covers its insides; the design system draws every control with radius 8 where Figma's Input Group is 10 (see the README).

Reply to a complaint/Badge.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font. Figma's 6 px sides are the Badge's 2 px padding plus its label's 4 px in code.

No match/Button.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font.

Template.$why: Figma's column hugs its content; code's fills the row beside the list.

Template/Title/Badge.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font. Figma's 6 px sides are the Badge's 2 px padding plus its label's 4 px in code.

Sentence.$why: Figma's sentence is a wrapping row of word frames (each 4 px wider than its word, rows 6 px apart); in code it is a paragraph with spaces, 28 px lines pulled in 4 px above and below, so the box is 56 px and takes 48.

Variable.$why: It grows with what is typed, whose width follows the font.

Variable#1.$why: It grows with what is typed. Being typed into, code draws the ring colour and the focus ring (as other fields do); Figma draws the input stroke.

Variable#1/TEXT.$why: An empty gap shows its name as the placeholder (muted); the check reads the input's own text colour.

Variable#2.$why: It grows with what is typed, whose width follows the font.

Variable#2/TEXT.$why: An empty gap shows its name as the placeholder (muted); the check reads the input's own text colour.

Footer.$why: Figma draws the 1 px line above the footer as its own layer; in code it is the footer's top border (45 px), so the card's height is the same.

Footer/Button.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font.

Footer/Button#1.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font.
